11. 30 g oxygen – 100 g of $\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_3$
48 g oxygen = $\frac{4800}{30}$
= 160 g of $\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_3$
Mass of metal = 160 – 48 = 112 g
$\therefore \mathrm{GAM} = \frac{112}{2} = 56$ g
Hence, the correct option is (d).

12. Volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ obtained at STP = 5.6 $l$
No. of moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2 = 0.25$ moles
$\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2$
No. of moles of $\mathrm{CaCO}_3 = 0.25 \times 100 = 25$ g
Amount of mixture = 50 g
Hence, the correct option is (b).

**13.** $2\mathrm{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{O}_2$
No. of moles of oxygen = $134.4/22.4 = 6$ moles
$6$ moles of $\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4$ moles of pure $\mathrm{KClO}_3$
$80\%$ of $x$ moles = $4$
$x = \frac{400}{80} = 5$ moles of pure $\mathrm{KClO}_3$
Extra amount of $\mathrm{KClO}_3$ taken
$= 5 - 4 = 1$ mole = $122.5$ g
Hence, the correct option is (d).

**14.** $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_2 + 5/2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
$\mathrm{CH}_4 + 2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
$\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4 + 3\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
$\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6 + 7/2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
(i) $\rightarrow$ (B); (ii) $\rightarrow$ (A); (iii) $\rightarrow$ (D); (iv) $\rightarrow$ (C)
Hence, the correct option is (b).

15. The balanced chemical equation for complete
combustion of hydrocarbon is
$\mathrm{C}_x\mathrm{H}_y + \left( x + \frac{y}{2} \right)\mathrm{O}_2 \to x\mathrm{CO}_2 + \frac{y}{2}\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

Given that $x + \frac{y}{4} = 4.5 \Rightarrow 4x + y = 18 \to$ (1)

Given that $x = \frac{y}{2} \Rightarrow y = 2x$
$\therefore$ From Eq. (1) $\Rightarrow 4x + 2x = 18 \Rightarrow x = 3$
$\therefore y = 2 \times 3 = 6$
$\therefore$ Hydrocarbon is $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6$.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

1. 44 g of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ corresponds to 1 mole, which con-
tains $6 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.
1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L at STP.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

2. The least possible temperature is $-273^\circ\mathrm{C}$ or
$0\ \mathrm{K}$. Any centigrade temperature greater than
$-273^\circ\mathrm{C}$ will become positive when converted
to absolute scale. Since centigrade temperature
less then $-273^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is not possible, Kelvin temper-
ature cannot have a negative value.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

3. Plumbic carbonate = $\mathrm{Pb}^{+4}$, $\mathrm{CO}^{-2}_3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{CO}_3)_2$
$\Rightarrow 6$ oxygen atoms
Ferric chromate = $\mathrm{Fe}^{+3}$, $\mathrm{CrO}_4^{-2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}_2(\mathrm{CrO}_4)_3$
$\Rightarrow 12$ oxygen atoms
Zinc silicate = $\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}$, $\mathrm{SiO}_3^{-2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{ZnSiO}_3 \Rightarrow 3$ oxy-
gen atoms
Aluminium sulphite = $\mathrm{Al}^{+3}$, $\mathrm{SO}_3^{-2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2 (\mathrm{SO}_3)_3$
$\Rightarrow 9$ oxygen atoms
Hence, the correct option is (b).

6. Oxyacid is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$.
$\therefore$ Negative radical is $\mathrm{SO}_4^{-2}$.
$\therefore$ Compound of $\mathrm{Fe}^{+3}$, $\mathrm{SO}_4^{-2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3$.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

7. Let $V_1 = 100\lambda, P_1 = 100$ atm

$V_2 = 70\lambda, P_2 =$?
According to Boyle's law $P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$

$\Rightarrow P_2 = \frac{P_1V_1}{V_2} = \frac{100 \times 100}{70} = 143$ atm
